title: The BEST Rogue rack accessory (Adjustable Monolift review)
summary: He reviews the Rogue adjustable monolift attachment after 8 months of weekly use. He uses it only for bench as a self lift-off: unracking heavy weight alone hurts the shoulders and wrecks setup. He covers 3x3 conversion, the screw-tightness quirk, wear on the plastic liner, and the price (about $120).

claims.claim: He has used the Rogue adjustable monolift every week for 8 months.

A rack-mounted monolift attachment costs about $100-120, versus a few thousand dollars for a dedicated monolift (e.g. Elite FTS), and can be moved for squat, OHP or bench, though moving it takes more effort than J-cups.
Rogue sells them for 3x4 racks; for a 3x3 rack buy Rogue's cheap conversion kit rather than forcing the 3x4 version or cutting metal. He loves 3x3 racks.
The arm only swings back under weight; with light loads (under about 135 lbs) it stays put.
A monolift lets you set up statically and skip the walkout on squats; he doesn't use it for squat or OHP because he finds walking out comfortable and likes it.

Unracking a heavy bench alone costs pounds, ruins setup and technique, and hurts the shoulders; many rotator cuff problems blamed on bench form actually come from the traumatic unrack and the difficulty of re-tucking afterwards.
With the monolift at the right height you just straighten your elbows and the arms slide clear; J-cups at that height would be hit on every rep.
He benches with a big arch and presses back towards the rack rather than straight up, and still never hits the monolift arms.
If you move the monolift between lifts, chalk-mark the holes so you don't have to work out positions each time.
If the arm stops short of full travel, the side screws have become too tight; loosen them slightly rather than returning it to Rogue.
The plastic liner grips the bar and wears down when you reposition heavy (300+ lb) bars; once worn through, steel contact can damage a quality barbell.
He recommends it to any home-gym owner without a spotter for lift-offs: it saves the shoulders and makes benching easier, and the hook angle makes missing the re-rack effectively impossible.
If you bench heavy at home, always set safety arms to catch the bar.
